reviews.review: The pinnacle of hacking simulations! An excellent simulation to experience what it could feel like, though not exact, to be a real-life hacker. An extensive gameplay, providing hours of fun, and a perfect game to wash away some free time! The game doesn't exactly provide a full analogy of what hacking would be like - for example programs for the simulated hacking are easier to obtain than they are in real life. But I'd definitely recommend this game!

wow. I had a TON of fun playing this game. There aren't many games that are addictive as this one that just have me want to play it so much. Having finally finished this game feels good, as I had a blast but also feels sad because, you know, this is the end.

Hacknet is a puzzle game and at the same time a hacking simulator. Game like these already exist but what makes hacknet special is that it offers an immersive experience with no hand holding. You have to dig inside the files of foreign computers, write down passwords that could be handy for later use. Read notes, read emails, use strategies learned by different people. You have to use your wits and think logically; what does the information that is given to me mean? Where can I find the information I need to complete the mission? You only know your goal, but how to achieve that is for you to figure out.
Hacknet does this amazingly as it's hard enough for you to feel accomplished when you finish the mission. You actually feel like you're getting better at this, you feel a growth in skill and knowledge. At the same time it's easy enough for it not to be frustrating. It doesn't feel impossible, everything can be found and there is always a way. If you can't seem to get it anyway, just a simple trace back and rereading your mission objective should be enough. Otherwise there are plenty of steam guides to help you out.

There also rewards for people that like to explore a lot and try things out besides the usual missions you take on. In fact, there is a "secret path" you can take for more missions.

Only downside of the game would probably be that it can be easy to break the game; with that I mean that an accidental removal of essential files could render some missions impossible to finish. Eventhough some missions can be aborted, some other way to prevent or cancel such mistakes would be great. 

Hacknet was good because it was challenging, yet fun. A more unique approach to puzzle games as a hacking game and also still interesting story made it very addicting. Definitely worth a buy!

Very fun, very interesting game about hacking. The story (especially Labyrinth's) explores a lot of the implications of hacking and what hacking makes possible (I suggest reading as many in-game documents as you can, most of the story details are in optional files).

Very fun to play, felt immersed the whole time. Yes, there are a lot of other "hacking" genre games that do it a lot more realistically where you have to have prior knowledge of hacking or coding in languages like javascript or python or whatever else, but this one keeps it simple, has a story that makes the player feel like they're actually involved in the in-game world, and has a soundtrack that hypes you up whenever you start hacking. 

TL;DR Good story, easy to learn gameplay, well fitting soundtrack.

[h1]WARNING this review will have spoilers, however, I've already marked what I consider to be spoilers[/h1]

This review is [b]NOT[/b] for people who plan on going through this game and only doing what the scripts you to. This is for those who want to delete everything they can get into after downloading files that they'd like to save as trophies or blackmail.

This is a great game, I have yet to beat it but I've loved most of the time I've put into this game, which is why I'm sad to say that I can't recommend this game. My main issue with it is the fact that its dead, unless I'm mistaken which is very possible. This game is filled with hand placed text and files as well as scripted events. At one point in the game, towards the beginning, [spoiler]you have to hack into a clicker game (that you can actually play which is super cool!) in order to delete an elite player's save so that he can show off his clicker power once more! I deleted the entire game alongside EVERYONE's saves. If you choose to do this you don't need to fret, you can still play the game, which is the main issue... WHY CAN I PLAY A DELETED GAME?[/spoiler] This trend follows with pretty much any computer or server you hack into, no one reacts, nothing gets repaired over time and things still work... WHY? Why does no one care if I've deleted ALL their system files, why do things still work even after I've deleted the file that basically says "DO NOT DELETE OR WILL STOP WORKING!!!" And why can't I blackmail people? I probably won't be able to get myself to beat this game because it just feels dead to me, sure its a lot of fun, but the immersion is killed the second I try to jump ship and do my own thing.

A second issue some people may have with this game is that it expects you to know, or figure out, everything outside of the few basic things it teachs you from the start, sometimes while being put under the clock. I have no real gripes with this, the game doesn't hold your hand (which I like), the only reason I mentioned it was for those players who don't like being forced to figure out solutions they've never been taught.

tl;dr: This game is dead, do anything outside of the script and its like nothing happened and no one cares. Make sure you can think on your feet and make sure you don't mind finding solutions to problems you've never even seen before.

This was the first good game about hacking that i ever have experienced.

Nice design overall, making you type a lot of stuff like you would do in a cmd/terminal, but also having visual interactive screens so you dont get bored of typing the same stuff over and over.
The story and concept are well explored and it feels really rewarding getting to the solution by ourselfs, it makes you feel smart. 

The dev did an absolutly amazing job with the extensions (modders), the extra levels and campains available on the workshop make this game so much better, It creates great replayability.

Most of the music tracks on the other hand were not so enjoyable to listen for long periods of time (too sharp sounds).
Now the downside of the game was guidence in the singleplayer campain (dlc was good tho). Yes, there was a huge amount fo text to read, but there are little things that aren't completly clarified (like for example not having the @entech.com in the e-mail login) that can get the player stuck.
I have spent at least more than half of the game just wondering endlessly because of small unclarified details.
Also it would be nicer to feel more at risk when leaving logs or getting traced.

Now in my opinion this is a good game, If the soundtrack and guidance were better this would be a great game. Even though there are some situations in the game that can drain the patience of the player and making it less fun, if you can ignore that, this is still an enjoyable experience.

If you're looking for a Hacking game, this would be my first pick of recommendation.

I think the best way for me to describe how good this game is is this:
I never replay story based games like Hacknet. Ever. There's an exception for games with multiple endings, but even then I find it incredibly boring to go through the same story again.
Then, I sat down to play Hacknet, after not playing it for 2 years (I spent 4 hours on it in 2016 but never finished it), played it for 4 hours straight, and got to the ending. And you know what I said after the credits rolled and the final cutscene played?
"I want to play that again."

Hacknet is an absolutely fantastic game. I fully recommend it to anyone.

Takes about 4 hours to get to the ending if you're fast (I had previous knowledge so I was faster than most). I haven't 100%ed it yet, but I can imagine it would take at least twice that. Soundtrack is 11/10, made me feel like a badass.
I'm now capable of hacking the FBI database. Thanks Hacknet.
